newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Typhoon Winnie kills one in Taiwan, gains strength.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Winnie kills one in Taiwan, gains strength.

text.p: Typhoon Winnie struck Taiwan on Monday, killing at least one person and bringing heavy torrential rains to the island, official said.
Police said one man drowned while fishing in a river in the northeastern county of Ilan, and another teenager was missing at a beach in eastern Taitung.
"North and northeastern Taiwan have entered Typhoon Winnie's range this morning... the typhoon is gaining strength," the Central Weather Bureau said.

Winnie, the first typhoon hit the island this year, was 300 km (186 miles) northeast of Taiwan's capital Taipei and moving west-north-west at 19 kph (12 miles) toward the island, the weather bureau said.

The typhoon, packing maximum sustained winds of 144 km per hour (89 miles per hour) and gusts of up to 180 kph (112 mph), forced government agencies, financial markets, schools and Taipei's domestic airport to close.
Strong wind and heavy rains also caused landslides, blocking some traffic in mountainous areas, officials said.
